title: Character Analysis & Frequency Counting Test Paper (ICSE Class X)
prerequisites: ICSE Class X String handling methods, Scanner input, conditional branching, and loops
instructions: All questions are compulsory as per ICSE examination standards.
Write complete Java code for Section B problems including Variable Description Tables.
Pay strict attention to case sensitivity, loop bounds, and array indexing.
Each question carries marks as indicated.

sections.description: Answer in one or two sentences or evaluate the code output.

questions.q: What is the return type and value of Character.isLetterOrDigit('@') in Java?
questions.answer: Return type is `boolean`, and the return value is `false` because '@' is a special punctuation character, not an alphabet letter or numerical digit.
questions.hint: Recall that symbols like @, #, $ are neither letters nor digits.

questions.q: State the difference between s.length() and arr.length in Java.
questions.answer: `s.length()` is a method call belonging to the java.lang.String class that returns the number of characters in a string. `arr.length` is an immutable field (attribute) of an array object that returns the capacity of the array.
questions.hint: Notice the parentheses () on the String version.

questions.q: Write a boolean condition to test if character variable 'ch' contains an uppercase alphabet without using any Character class methods.
questions.answer:
```java
if (ch >= 'A' && ch <= 'Z')
```
This uses the Unicode/ASCII range 65 to 90 directly.

questions.q: What integer value is returned by "AEIOUaeiou".indexOf('k')?
questions.answer:
Output: `-1`
Explanation: When the character or substring is not found inside the calling string, indexOf() always returns -1.
questions.hint: When a search character is missing, indexOf returns a negative constant.

sections.description: Write complete Java programs with class declaration, main method, and Variable Description Table.

questions.q:
Write a program in Java to accept a sentence from the user. Count and display:
(i) Number of uppercase letters
(ii) Number of lowercase letters
(iii) Number of digits
(iv) Number of special characters
Include a Variable Description Table.
questions.hint: Loop through length(), check with Character methods, and maintain 4 separate counters.

questions.q: Write a program to accept a string in uppercase and count the individual frequency of each vowel (A, E, I, O, U) present in the string.
questions.hint: Use a switch-case statement inside the traversal loop to tally each vowel.
